scope: free/open curriculum + reusable learning artifacts for OpenMAIC
rights_disclaimer: Not legal advice. License strings are verbatim quotes from pages fetched on the retrieval date. 'unknown' means not verified, never 'permitted'. AI summarisation does not remove underlying license conditions.

sources.name: OpenStax (Rice University)
sources.license: MIXED per-book: CC BY 4.0 (38 titles) and CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (80 titles), 11 unresolved
sources.license_quote: "license_name": "Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike License" / "license_name": "Creative Commons Attribution License" (per-book field, OpenStax CMS API, 129 books enumerated)

sources.authorship_evidence: Named academic author/reviewer teams per book; peer-reviewed; Rice University nonprofit publisher

sources.exceptions: Per-title license differs between editions: 'College Physics' = CC BY but 'College Physics 2e' = CC BY-NC-SA. Newer editions trend NC. Third-party images inside books often carry separate rights. Instructor answer keys/test banks are access-gated, NOT openly licensed.

sources.integration: Highest-value scene/lesson text source. Ingest ONLY the 38 CC BY titles for any commercial path; gate the NC titles behind a non-commercial flag or exclude. Section prose -> slide scenes; end-of-section exercises -> quiz scene items.

sources.authorship_evidence: Illustrative Mathematics nonprofit; named curriculum authors; EdReports-reviewed (review rating not verified here)

sources.integration: Best structured-lesson source in the catalogue: lesson->activity->task maps almost 1:1 to OpenMAIC scene sequences, and practice problems feed quiz scenes with real answer keys.

sources.name: Wikibooks / Wikiversity (Wikimedia)
sources.license: CC BY-SA 4.0, most text dual-licensed GFDL
sources.license_quote: Most of Wikibooks' text is dual licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License ("CC BY-SA 4.0") and the GNU Free Documentation License (GFDL) (unversioned, with no invariant sections, front-cover texts, or back-cover texts).

sources.authorship_evidence: WEAKEST editorial provenance in the catalogue — volunteer, no editorial board, quality varies per book. Treat as raw material needing curation.
sources.commercial_note: TRUE but SHARE-ALIKE: derivative lessons must be released under CC BY-SA. This is viral into your generated content if you adapt the text.
sources.exceptions: Some text CC BY-SA-only and not GFDL-reusable. Embedded images carry independent licenses (check Commons per file). Per-page footer is authoritative.
sources.access: Full MediaWiki Action API + XML dumps (machine-readable, no scraping needed)
sources.integration: Use for long-tail/expert topics where no vetted OER exists. ShareAlike makes it unsuitable as the base layer of proprietary generated lessons — keep in a separately-licensed content partition.

sources.name: Project Gutenberg
sources.license: Public domain (US) works + PG trademark license
sources.license_quote: Nearly all the individual works in the collection are in the public domain in the United States.
sources.artifact_types: full-text books (TXT/HTML/EPUB), bulk catalogue feeds
sources.authorship_evidence: Original authors are historical/canonical; PG transcription is volunteer but proofread (Distributed Proofreaders)
sources.commercial_note: TRUE for the underlying public-domain text. Strip the PG header/trademark and the text is unrestricted; keep the header and you accept the PG trademark license terms.
sources.exceptions: PG explicitly declines to call its corpus 'public domain' wholesale. Non-US copyright status differs (life+70 in EU). A minority of items are copyrighted-with-permission. The PG trademark itself is NOT public domain.
sources.access: Bulk catalogue (CSV/RDF), per-book plain text, rsync mirrors — ideal offline
sources.integration: Reading-passage source for literacy/comprehension scenes and ES/EN parallel reading. Pair with generated comprehension questions (your questions, their text).

sources.name: Standard Ebooks

sources.authorship_evidence: Volunteer-produced but strict documented style manual and multi-stage review; cleanest machine-readable classic texts available
sources.commercial_note: TRUE, unrestricted — CC0 is the single cleanest rights position in this catalogue.
sources.exceptions: Only covers public-domain source works; US-centric PD determination
sources.access: GitHub repos per book (semantic XHTML), EPUB downloads, OPDS feed
sources.integration: Prefer over raw Gutenberg where the title exists: semantic XHTML parses into clean paragraph/chapter scene units with zero attribution burden.

sources.name: LibreTexts

sources.authorship_evidence: UC Davis-led consortium, NSF/DoE-funded, named faculty curators per text
sources.commercial_note: FALSE for the observed default (NC). Per-page license tag is machine-readable ('license:ccbyncsa','licenseversion:40') — some pages are CC BY or PD, so item-level filtering is possible and REQUIRED.
sources.exceptions: Every page carries its own license tag; the collection cannot be treated as one license. Content is itself remixed from upstream sources whose conditions persist.

sources.integration: Only ingest after filtering on the per-page license tag. The machine-readable tag makes an automated rights gate feasible — this is the one large collection where you can mechanically prove each page's license.

sources.name: Siyavula (Everything Maths/Science)

sources.exceptions: The branded/unbranded distinction is the whole rights question. ND on branded versions blocks the adaptation your product depends on. Must confirm which download corresponds to which license before ingestion.
sources.access: Public web read; PDF downloads; no API verified
sources.integration: Strong for secondary maths/science with worked solutions. Use unbranded CC BY files only. Good offline candidate (PDF/print heritage).

sources.authorship_evidence: STRONGEST editorial signal available: faculty peer reviews with named reviewers and rubric scores per book
sources.commercial_note: UNKNOWN per book — it is a DIRECTORY, not a licensor. The CC BY applies to UMN's own catalogue pages, not to the books.
sources.exceptions: Mislabelling risk: 'found in Open Textbook Library' does not mean CC BY. Each book's license must be read at its own host.
sources.access: Public web; no API verified
sources.integration: Use as the QUALITY GATE / discovery index, not as a content source: pick books by peer-review score, then resolve rights at the publisher.

sources.integration: Best fit for the ADULT LITERACY / upgrading audience. Pressbooks exports give structured XHTML chapters that map to scene units with little parsing work.

sources.name: WeBWorK Open Problem Library
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0
sources.license_quote: [![](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-CC%20BY--NC--SA%203.0-blue)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0/)

sources.authorship_evidence: MAA/NSF-supported; university mathematics faculty contributors; per-problem metadata

sources.access: Full git repo clone; structured OPL-DB taxonomy; per-problem .pg source
sources.integration: DO NOT ingest for a commercial product. Its real value is as a STRUCTURE model: the parameterized-problem pattern (randomized values + answer checker) is what your quiz scene generator should imitate with your own items.

sources.name: Numbas (Newcastle University)
sources.license: SOFTWARE Apache 2.0; shared question CONTENT = per-item CC licenses
sources.license_quote: All of the Numbas software is open source, available under the Apache 2.0 licence.
sources.artifact_types: parameterized question bank, SCORM/standalone HTML exam packages, JSON question definitions
sources.authorship_evidence: Newcastle University School of Mathematics; actively maintained (GitHub API confirms repo + editor repo both Apache-2.0)
sources.commercial_note: SPLIT: software Apache-2.0 = commercially usable (verified). Public question DATABASE items are 'shared under Creative Commons licences' — plural, per-item, NOT verified individually. Do not treat the question bank as uniformly reusable.
sources.exceptions: Classic code-vs-content trap. Verified quote: 'Reuse the thousands of tests and individual questions shared under Creative Commons licences in the public database' — which CC variant is per item.
sources.access: GitHub (Apache-2.0), Numbas editor API, exports standalone HTML + SCORM
sources.integration: Best BUILD-ON option for exams: Apache-2.0 engine you can legally embed, authoring your own items, instead of ingesting NC question banks. Exports run offline.

sources.commercial_note: GPL-3.0 is copyleft SOFTWARE: usable commercially but linking/distribution obligations attach to your code. Legal review needed before embedding in a proprietary app.
sources.exceptions: GPL obligations are about your SOFTWARE, not content. Requires a Maxima CAS runtime — real infrastructure cost.
sources.access: GitHub repo, Moodle plugin
sources.integration: SKIP for now: GPL copyleft + Maxima dependency is heavy infrastructure, and the brief forbids new platforms. Note as the reference design for symbolic answer-grading.

sources.name: Kolibri / Learning Equality

sources.integration: DIRECTLY serves the offline + low-literacy + multilingual requirements, and its per-node license metadata is the model for your own rights gate. Query the channel API for CC BY channels.

sources.integration: Default VISUAL asset source for diagrams and illustrations in slide/diagram scenes. API license metadata allows an automated CC0/PD/CC BY-only filter.

Therefore, attribution of the information directly to NASA is not permitted.' Any AI-adapted NASA content must NOT be attributed to NASA.
